summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of recurrent perianal abscesses was admitted for fevers, headache, joint pain, and malaise that began two weeks prior. Initial evaluation revealed no infectious source—lumbar puncture, blood cultures, chest X-ray, and head CT were all negative. CT pelvis showed mild perirectal inflammation but no abscess. Laboratory tests showed elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 78.1, ESR 41), supporting a lupus flare. She developed oral ulcers during admission and was started on prednisone 15 mg daily. Her symptoms improved, she remained afebrile for over 24 hours, and was discharged home with follow-up in primary care, rheumatology, and orthopedics. Medication changes included initiation of prednisone and viscous lidocaine for mouth pain.
